recommendation: Keep the source fix as-is. It completes the originally published correction in the active Binary narrative without changing broader Binary behavior.
issue_request: FHIR-17024 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core Binary correction raised against STU3. It asked to replace scope wording that said Binary resources could be represented in XML or JSON with wording covering XML, JSON, or other FHIR formats and clarifying that the content is represented as base64-encoded content.
initial_application: The issue was initially applied by git-svn commit 2941d0f9788c72cfa11ca22a381c2157e87eef9f / svn 14347, which changed the Binary scope text from "XML or JSON" to "XML, JSON, of other formats" and fixed an unrelated punctuation typo. Commit 7bf7397f4a965784698e0d343f8a96789cdf4942 later corrected "of" to "or", leaving the all-formats part applied but still omitting the requested base64 clarification.
additional_context: Binary is actively listed in source/fhir.ini, so source/binary/binary-introduction.xml is current build source. Binary.data is already defined as base64Binary with the definition "The actual content, base64 encoded," confirming the requested narrative clarification is consistent with the conformance source. Targeted Zulip and Confluence searches found no direct discussion or later decision that supersedes the Jira/source conclusion.
reconciliation: Updated source/binary/binary-introduction.xml to say Binary resources can be represented in XML, JSON, or other formats as base64-encoded data, preserving the native REST-interface distinction and Bundle example.
source_changes: source/binary/binary-introduction.xml: clarified that XML, JSON, and other FHIR-format Binary representations carry base64-encoded data.
